releaseName: Cover letters that read like you wrote them
summary: Cover letters now draw on the facts that best match the job, avoid sentences that only name a skill, and use fewer stock phrases (#2583). A server can switch to writing a letter as plain prose and then checking each sentence against your career facts: unsupported sentences get one rewrite and are otherwise left out and listed (DRAFT_LOOP_COVER_LETTER_WRITER=free-form; #2584, #2585, #2586). The Prepare panel is easier to reach: a Cover letter or interview button opens it, its Draft button names the open tab, and employer findings fold away (#2578, #2591, #2595). A Markdown export preview shows only the Markdown text (#2580). A job page's saved copy is kept and shown in the Job tab, and a job without one can get a copy or pasted text (#2594, #2596).
knownLimitations: The free-form cover letter writer is off unless a server sets DRAFT_LOOP_COVER_LETTER_WRITER=free-form, and the blind test that would make it the default (#2483) has not run yet. On the hosted staging service, drafting needs model screening, which stays off there until Claude on Vertex AI is available. A research run costs at most US$0.20 and reads search results only. Agents still cannot approve, export or start paid runs. French is beta until the French quality gate (milestone 83) runs. The local-first desktop has no career interview or Prepare panel.
